verdicts.claim: Requirements written as statements (shall, must, should, will provide, Vendor to confirm, Support for, REQ-101, 3.2.4, Ability to, R1.) are not found at all (Opus A1, Gemini 1, DeepSeek 1).
verdicts.evidence: All ten inputs run one at a time: count=0 each, status "pasted.txt: no questions found. RFP questions usually end with a question mark or start with words like describe, provide or explain." All ten in one paste: count=0; paragraphs() also glued "REQ-101: ..." onto the end of "3.6 Support for scheduled publishing." (out_C1.1.json).
verdicts.cause: findQuestions keeps a paragraph only when the body contains "?" or a sentence starts with an ASKS verb (/^(describe|explain|provide|...|please)\b/i), so a declarative requirement never passes the `asks` gate at line 134, and NUM gives "REQ-101" and "R1." no label either.
verdicts.fix: Agree with the reviewers: add a REQUIREMENT test beside ASKS (\b(shall|must|should|will|is required to|ability to|support for|capable of)\b) for numbered or coded lines, and let NUM accept coded ids (REQ-101, FR-3.2, R1.); a statement found this way should be tagged so the draft can answer "we would meet this by" instead of "our approach".

verdicts.claim: Mandatory and desirable tags delete the question; only "...programs. (Mandatory)" survives with the tag inside the text (Opus A2); M1 (Mandatory) and D1 (Desirable) are treated as ordinary questions (DeepSeek 5).
verdicts.evidence: One at a time: 2.1 (M), 2.2 [Mandatory], 2.3 MANDATORY:, 2.4 Desirable -, [M] 2.5, M1 (Mandatory), D1 (Desirable) all count=0; only 2.6 survives, label "2.6", text "Describe how you would set up Marketo programs. (Mandatory)", kind adobe, products [marketo], lines MK06, MK01, MK02, MK05. All eight in one paste: count=1, and the survivor's text becomes "Describe how you would set up Marketo programs. (Mandatory) M1 (Mandatory) The solution must support SSO." because paragraphs() glued the unnumbered M1 line onto it; "[M] 2.5" glued onto 2.4 and both vanished. DeepSeek's prediction that M1 and D1 are kept as ordinary questions is wrong: they are dropped (out_C1.2.json).
verdicts.cause: The ASKS regex is anchored at the start of each sentence, so a tag before the verb ("(M) Describe", "[Mandatory] Describe", "MANDATORY: Explain", "Desirable - Describe") fails it; NUM does not recognise "[M]", "M1" or "D1" as labels, and a trailing "(Mandatory)" is never stripped, while paragraphs() glues any unnumbered line onto a previous paragraph shorter than 80 characters.
verdicts.fix: Agree: strip a leading or trailing M/D tag ((M), [M], MANDATORY:, Mandatory, Desirable, (D)) before the ASKS test and keep it in its own field on the question (and in the Excel export); treat "M1", "D1" as labels in NUM.

verdicts.claim: Sub-questions: the parent "12. We are implementing AJO and RTCDP" is dropped; a) is kept but matches only rtcdp; b) gets no catalog match although JO03 IP warmup exists (Gemini 3); "4.1 Describe: a) ...; b) ...; c) ..." yields one question and loses b and c (DeepSeek 4); (i) (ii) (iii) lose their parent and get labels like "(i" (Opus A14).

Answer it yourself, or move it to Your firm..."; b) label "b", kind unsure, products [], same No match panel, although RFP_CAT.lines.JO03 = "IP warmup plan execution" exists (in ajo.more); c) label "c", products [rtcdp, ajo], conn rtcdp+ajo, lines XA02, XA01, JO05, RT03. verdicts.cause: paragraphs() makes a) b) c) and (i) their own paragraphs via NUM and findQuestions drops the parent stem's statement (no ASKS verb) and never passes its words down, so detect() sees no product; "ip warmup", "sandboxes" and "subdomains" are in no ALIASES entry and JO03 is an optional line in ajo.more that match() keeps only when the question names a distinctive word of its name; the label strip `m[0].trim().replace(/[.)]$/,'')` removes the closing bracket but not the opening one.
verdicts.fix: Agree on the direction: carry the stem (a numbered line that ends with ":" or a statement directly above lettered items) into each sub-item's text for detect() and match(), label them "12 a", add ip warmup, subdomains and sandboxes to ALIASES.ajo and rtcdp, strip both brackets from labels, and drop a stem that has no words after the colon; Gemini's rtcdp claim for a) is not what the code does (no product at all).

verdicts.claim: Lot headings: 1.1 gets No match, the Lot 2 heading glues onto 1.2 which is answered as CJA, and 2.1 disappears as a duplicate of 1.1 (Opus A14).
verdicts.evidence: count=3 of 4 numbered questions. paragraphs(): ["Lot 1: Adobe Experience Manager Sites", "1.1 Describe your implementation approach.", "1.2 Describe your approach to ongoing support. Lot 2: Customer Journey Analytics", "2.1 ...", "2.2 ..."]. #0 label 1.1, kind adobe, products [], panel "No match in the catalog for this question"; #1 label 1.2, text "Describe your approach to ongoing support. Lot 2: Customer Journey Analytics", products [cja], lines C06, CJ03, draft "We would deliver this with Customer Journey Analytics... define up to five audiences from AI-referred visits..."; 2.1 absent; #2 label 2.2, products [cja] fromContext, lines [], whole draft "Our approach / After launch, across the Adobe products in this proposal, our ongoing services for Customer Journey Analytics are these." and nothing follows (out_C1.4.json, out_followup.json).
verdicts.cause: paragraphs() flushes an unnumbered line only when the previous paragraph ends a sentence, the line starts with a capital and the previous paragraph is over 80 characters, so the 41-character 1.2 swallows "Lot 2: ..."; findQuestions dedupes on the body text alone (key at line 137, label excluded) so 2.1 equals 1.1; a Lot heading is never kept as context.
verdicts.fix: Agree: treat "Lot N:", "Section N" and similar headings as section starts (add to the `starts` test) and attach the current heading to each question for detect() and match(); dedupe on label plus body, or keep repeats and mark them "same wording as 1.1".

verdicts.claim: The instruction filter deletes real questions: "Submit a migration plan...", "Describe how Brand Concierge would answer all of our members' questions...", "Describe how Workfront alerts campaign owners when a deadline is at risk." and the fragment "The system alerts campaign owners when a deadline is at risk." (Opus A15).
verdicts.evidence: All four: count=0, status "no questions found". INSTRUCTION.exec: "Submit" (alternative ^submit\b) on the first; "answer all of our members' questions" (alternative \b(respond|reply|answer)\b.*\b(each|every|all)\b.*\b(question|item|section)s?\b) on the second; "deadline" (\bdeadline\b) on the third. The fourth also matches "deadline" but is dropped one line earlier by the `asks` gate (ASKS.test=false: it is a statement), so for that fragment the filter is not the reason (out_C1.5.json, out_C1.5_regex.json).
verdicts.cause: findQuestions line 136, `if(!/\?/.test(body)&&INSTRUCTION.test(body))continue;`, drops any question without a question mark when INSTRUCTION matches anywhere in it: ^submit\b, the answer...all...questions chain, and the unanchored \bdeadline\b.
verdicts.fix: Agree: anchor the filter to whole-paragraph instructions (require the match at the start of the body, drop the bare \bdeadline\b and let ^submit only fire when followed by your/the proposal|response|bid), and never apply it to a body that starts with an ASKS verb other than submit.

verdicts.claim: Silent limits: (a) 350 numbered lines show 300 found with no warning; (b) a question over 900 characters is dropped; (c) REQ-001, FR-3.2 and Item 15: numbering is dropped; (d) "Please note that all responses become the property of..." appears as a question; (e) French, Spanish and Portuguese questions are dropped (Opus A22, A24, Gemini 9); (f) a yes/no security appendix is under-classified (DeepSeek 7).

(b) a 1,194-character question naming AEM Sites: count=0, status "no questions found"; the same text cut to under 900 characters: count=1. Describe your data retention policy." (kind adobe via WORK "customer data", no draft): the heading and S1 glue, S2 and S3 glue, no row is labelled, nothing is drafted (out_C1.6a.json to out_C1.6f.json).
verdicts.cause: findQuestions: `if(p.length<12||p.length>900)continue;` (line 131) and `if(qs.length>=300)break;` (line 140) with no message in status(); NUM has no form for "REQ-001", "FR-3.2", "Item 15:" or "S1.", and ASKS is anchored to the sentence start so the code-prefixed body fails; ASKS accepts ^please so a notice starting with "Please" survives; ASKS is English only; classify() has no security or appendix rule, so WORK's "customer data" puts S2/S3 in Adobe services.
verdicts.fix: Agree: raise the caps (or page them) and say "N more lines were not read" in the status line; let NUM take coded ids (letters, digits, dashes, a colon); treat "Please note" as a notice; a yes/no row (starts with do you|does|is|are|can) with no product should go to Your firm or the planned knowledge base; languages need a proper verb list per language, which is out of scope for a regex finder and worth saying on the page.

verdicts.claim: Two-part questions lose one part: "...AEM Sites and the team you would assign" goes to Your firm with no AEM draft; "...including a timeline and staffing plan" gets no timeline or staffing; "Describe your experience implementing Adobe Experience Manager Sites for banks." gets a build plan instead of experience (Opus A21).
verdicts.evidence: (1) kind firm, draft null (status "1 about your firm"). (2) kind adobe, products [aemsites], lines SI02, SI01, SI05, SI06; the full draft contains neither "timeline" nor "staff" (regex checks false); it reads "We would deliver this with AEM Sites. / We will build the site from the AEM Project Archetype or a Site Template...". (3) kind adobe, lines SI01, SI02, SI04, SI05: "We will assign AEM product profiles in the Admin Console, create the production program and environments in Cloud Manager...", a build plan with no reference or experience content (out_C1.7.json, out_followup.json).
verdicts.cause: classify() tests FIRM before ADOBE, so "the team" (\b(your|the|our) (...)?(team)\b) wins the whole question; compose() builds every draft from matched service lines, so a timeline, staffing or past-experience part has no source and is silently left out.
verdicts.fix: Agree: when both FIRM and ADOBE match, keep the Adobe draft and add a "Your part to write" box naming the firm part (team, timeline, staffing, experience, references); a question that starts with "Describe your experience" should go to Your firm even when it names a product.

extra.claim: Unnumbered questions on their own lines glue into one question when the previous one is under 80 characters.

Paste "Do you support SSO?
Do you encrypt data at rest?
What is your uptime SLA?
Describe your approach to AEM Sites.": paragraphs() returns one paragraph, count=1, text "Do you support SSO? Do you encrypt data at rest? What is your uptime SLA? Describe your approach to AEM Sites.", kind adobe, drafted as AEM Sites (SI02, SI01, SI05, SI06). extra.claim: Common RFP request openers are not in ASKS, so the question is dropped: Briefly describe, Respondents must describe, Bidders are asked to explain, In no more than 300 words describe, Kindly outline, The vendor should describe.
extra.evidence: Six such lines pasted as separate paragraphs: count=0, status "no questions found" (out_X2.json). Cause: ASKS is anchored to the sentence start (^(describe|explain|...)\b) and has no adverb or subject forms. Fix: allow an optional lead-in (briefly|kindly|please|in no more than ... ,|respondents?|bidders?|vendors?|the vendor|proposers?) (must|should|shall|are asked to|are required to)? before the verb.

extra.claim: Upper-case bracketed sub-items (A), (B) are not recognised as labels and are dropped.

Cause: NUM's bracketed form `(\(?[a-z0-9]{1,3}\))` is lower-case only and the regex has no /i flag, so "(A) Describe" fails ASKS. Fix: [A-Za-z0-9] in that alternative.

Describe how you would:\n- migrate content to AEM Sites\n- connect AEM Sites to Target": count=1, text "Describe how you would:", label 5, kind unsure, no draft; the two bullets vanish (out_X6.json; same in C1.3 roman). extra.evidence: "1. Why us?\n2. Why AEM?\n3. Describe your approach to AEM Sites.": count=1 (only item 3) (out_X7.json). Cause: `if(p.length<12||p.length>900)continue;` measures the whole paragraph including the label. Fix: apply the minimum to the body after the label and lower it to about 6.

extra.claim: A two-sentence question on two lines splits into two questions when the first sentence is over 80 characters, and the second half lands in Not sure with no draft.

extra.claim: An ongoing-services question answered from context can produce a draft that promises a list and gives none.
extra.evidence: C1.4 question 2.2 "Describe your approach to ongoing support.": products [cja] fromContext, lines [], the entire client-facing draft is "Our approach / After launch, across the Adobe products in this proposal, our ongoing services for Customer Journey Analytics are these." with no items and no sources; panel shows it with Use this answer enabled (out_followup.json C14_q22). Cause: match() with fromContext keeps only monthly lines (`if(fromContext&&!monthly)continue;`) and skips the fallback (`!fromContext`), and compose() returns a draft whenever m.products is non-empty. Fix: in compose(), return null (No match) when fromContext and m.lines is empty.

verdicts.claim: An Excel compliance matrix (Req ID | Category | Requirement | Priority | Comply | Vendor response, two sheets) collapses: FR rows vanish, ID/Category/Priority glue onto rows, SEC rows merge with the header; pasted as tabs it becomes one question drafted as AEM Sites + Target.
verdicts.evidence: requirements.xlsx -> status '1 question found. 0 about Adobe services, 0 about your firm, 1 to sort'; the one item: label '', text 'Req ID Category Requirement Priority Comply (Y/N/P) Vendor response SEC-01 Security Do you support single sign-on with SAML 2.0?', pile Not sure. FR-01 to FR-06 all vanish (two start with Describe). Paragraphs show the glue: 'M FR-02 Content The solution shall support multi-site management across 12 brands.' and 'M FR-03 Content Describe your approach to migrating content into AEM Sites. M FR-04 Hosting The platform must publish to a CDN with purge on publish.' Difference from Opus: 1 item not 2; SEC-02 ('M SEC-02 Security Describe your data retention policy. M') is dropped rather than merged, which depends on the Priority cell. Pasted as tab-separated text in one block: 1 question (the whole 743-char matrix), pile Adobe, products cja, target, aemsites, connection aemsites+target, lines AXB02, AXB03, CJ01, C06, text starts 'Our approach - AEM Sites exports Experience Fragments (HTML or JSON) and Content Fragments (JSON) to Target as offers...'. With a blank line between the two sheets: the whole FR block vanishes and only the SEC block survives as one unsure item.
verdicts.cause: readSheet pushes every cell as its own line and joins a cell to the next only under the rule `if(/^\(?[A-Za-z]?\d{0,3}(\.\d+)*[.)]?$/.test(cells[i])&&cells[i].length<=8&&i+1<cells.length){lines.push(cells[i].replace(/[.)]$/,'')+' '+cells[i+1]);i++;}` (FR-01, SEC-01, REQ-04 fail on the hyphen and second letter); paragraphs() then glues the lines back (it breaks only on a NUM-start line, or a capitalised line after a sentence end once the paragraph is over 80 chars), and findQuestions tests ASKS only at a sentence start, which is now the ID or the header text.
verdicts.fix: Agree with all three reviewers: read sheets (and tab-separated pastes) row by row, find the header row by column names (ID, Category, Requirement/Question, Priority, Comply, Response) or take the longest text column as the question, and emit one structured item per data row {label, category, priority, text}, skipping header rows; this is cleaner than widening the numbering regex.

verdicts.claim: The row REQ-04 | Analytics | Describe how CJA joins paid media data with web conversions. | Mandatory loses its ID and Mandatory tag; and a Category cell 'Explain how you handle security' beside a Requirement 'System must support SSO' is captured as the question while the requirement is dropped.

Without the header row: also 'no questions found' (paragraph 'REQ-04 Analytics Describe how Customer Journey Analytics joins paid media data with web conversions.'). The requirement is lost whole, not kept without its ID. Trap REQ-05 | Explain how you handle security | System must support SSO | Mandatory: nothing found, with or without the header. Trap with a numeric ID 4.2: label '4.2', text 'Explain how you handle security System must support SSO Mandatory', pile Not sure: the category heads the question text and the requirement is glued in after it, not dropped.
verdicts.cause: Same readSheet numbering rule plus paragraphs() joining and the ASKS sentence-start anchor; with '4.2' the rule joins the ID to the next cell, which is the Category, and the Requirement and Priority cells are appended.
verdicts.fix: Agree on the direction (structured row ingestion as in C2.1); the question text must come from the Requirement column alone, with Category kept as a field.

Question

Response

Describe your approach to implementing AEM Sites.

verdicts.claim: A CSV with a quoted multiline cell ("R-1","The system must\nsupport real-time activation","") breaks on naive splitting into two items.
verdicts.evidence: SheetJS parses the quoted newline as one cell: rows [['ID','Requirement','Response'],['R-1','The system must\nsupport real-time activation',''],['R-2','Describe your approach to implementing Adobe Target.','']]; readSheet's join makes it two lines but paragraphs() rejoins them into 'The system must support real-time activation'. The file yields 'multiline.csv: no questions found': the whole CSV is one paragraph 'ID Requirement Response R-1 The system must support real-time activation R-2 Describe your approach to implementing Adobe Target.', so even R-2's Describe question is lost. With numeric IDs: '2 Describe your approach to implementing Adobe Target.' is found (label 2, Target, lines TG01, TG02, TG03, TG05) and '1 The system must support real-time activation' is one paragraph, dropped as declarative.
verdicts.cause: The CSV parse is right; the loss is readSheet's numbering rule rejecting 'R-1' and 'R-2', so the IDs become lines that paragraphs() glues onto the sentence start where ASKS fails. DeepSeek's aside that no XLSX reader ships is wrong: lib/xlsx.mini.min.js loads on first use and reads CSV.

verdicts.claim: PDFs: a question that runs onto the next page is cut and its second half becomes an unnumbered row, running headers glue in garbled; a PDF table drops the declarative row; a scanned PDF says 'no questions found' instead of naming the missing text layer.
verdicts.evidence: (a) split.pdf: '6 questions found'; 3.4 text ends '...to Brand Visibility, and which teams on our side' (Adobe, cja + bv); the next item is label '', text 'Northbridge Mutual Bank RFP 2026 Page 2 would need to be involved?', pile Not sure; 3.5 found. The header is glued in but not garbled when the PDF comes from reportlab (one pdf.js item per line, even a glyph-by-glyph header was merged by pdf.js). It is garbled from a Chromium-printed letter-spaced header (chromium_header.pdf): 'N O R T H B R I D G E M U T U A L B A N K R F P 2 0 2 6 P A G E 2 would need to be involved?' (pdf.js returns one item per glyph plus ' ' items). (b) table.pdf: the row's cells come through on one line '3.4   The solution shall support multi-site management across 12 regional brands.'; 3.4 dropped, 3.5 found with its label: '1 question found'. (c) scan.pdf: readPdf returns '\n\n'; status 'scan.pdf: no questions found. RFP questions usually end with a question mark or start with words like describe, provide or explain. Try pasting the questions section.'
verdicts.cause:
readPdf: `const y=Math.round(it.transform[5]); if(lastY!==null&&Math.abs(y-lastY)>2){text+=line.trim()+'
';line='';} line+=it.str+(it.hasEOL?'
':' ');lastY=y;` then per page `text+=line.trim()+'

';` so a page end is a paragraph break, the running header is the first line of the next paragraph, and every item gets a trailing space; load() has a single message for an empty result.
verdicts.fix: Agree with Opus: in readPdf drop lines that repeat on most pages (running headers and footers), join a page's last line to the next page's first line when that line does not start a numbered item, add a space only when the next item is not adjacent (pdf.js already emits ' ' items), and when no page yields a text item say the PDF has no text layer and needs OCR or pasted text.

verdicts.claim: Only the first file of a multi-file drop is read.
verdicts.evidence: A DragEvent with a two-file DataTransfer (bank_rfp.xlsx, retail_rfi.docx) on #rfp-drop: status 'bank_rfp.xlsx: 14 questions found. 8 about Adobe services, 6 about your firm...'; reversed: 'retail_rfi.docx: 8 questions found...'; the second file is never mentioned. page.setInputFiles('#rfp-file', [both]) is refused by Playwright: 'Non-multiple file input can only accept single file', because the input has no multiple attribute, so the chooser can only ever pick one file.
verdicts.cause: `drop.addEventListener('drop',e=>{const f=e.dataTransfer&&e.dataTransfer.files&&e.dataTransfer.files[0];take(f);});` and `$r('rfp-file').addEventListener('change',e=>{const f=e.target.files[0];e.target.value='';take(f);});` both take files[0].
verdicts.fix: Agree: read every dropped file in turn and append its questions under its file name (and add multiple to the input), or at least say in the status that only the first file was read.

(Query Service lowercased); 1 colon clause with a subject: AD1 "For the agreed ad accounts (...): we will your ad admins approve access in each network; we authorizes the Experience Platform advertising sources". Gemini's BI2 and AD2 reproduced. rfp() sweep over 201 scopes, 75 how, 75 gain.text, all prereqs and sowPrereqs: 16 regex hits; in text that reaches the client 10, of which 6 real: scopes O05 "partner-designed improvements", C05 "a partner-managed handoff", CW01 "the Adobe/partner/Client responsibility split", C03 "a partner-managed handoff", C02 "a partner validation sheet", and cja-bc gain.text "a partner can analyze the Concierge events"; 4 false positives ("the customer ID" in CR1 and crm-target, "the customer profile" in aemsites-rtcdp and marketo-rtcdp). Opus's six matched. Gemini's three examples do not: O04 outputs "we does not edit articles about you directly" (not "the partner ... the client"); cw-cja outputs "our Skills turn your agreed AI-channel measures" (not "the client's"); marketo-ajo "provisioned for the customer" is prereqs[1], shown unrewritten in the partner note only.
